title: Designing portfolio projects like product case studies
description: How to move beyond screenshots and explain problem, tradeoffs, implementation, and measurable outcomes.
hero: A project card shows what was built. A case study shows how you think. The difference matters when a portfolio is meant to communicate professional maturity.

sections.heading: Lead with the product problem
body: A strong case study starts before the interface. It explains the user need, business constraint, technical limitation, or workflow problem that made the work necessary.
This gives the reader a reason to care about the implementation choices that follow.

sections.heading: Explain tradeoffs clearly
body: Every interface is a chain of decisions. A senior portfolio should make those decisions visible: why this layout, why this state model, why this navigation pattern, and what was intentionally left out.
Tradeoffs are proof of judgment. They show that the developer was not just assembling screens.

sections.heading: End with impact
body: Impact can be quantitative, but it does not always have to be. For personal projects, impact can mean improved scan speed, cleaner state ownership, stronger accessibility, or a more maintainable component model.
The key is to connect the result back to the original problem.

takeaways: Frame projects around problems, not tools.
Connect outcomes to the reason the project exists.
